transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been eating a lot more than I mean to, mostly after work or class. I’ll sit down with my laptop and end up having a whole takeout meal, then chips, sweets, and whatever snacks I have in my desk drawer. It’s way more than I’d eat around other people.
After one of these eating episodes, do you ever do anything to try to make up for it—like make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise a lot to compensate?
I’m not sure what you mean by make up for it. I usually just feel bad afterward.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah. Once I start, it feels like I’m just watching myself keep reaching for the next thing. I’m thinking, “Jaime, stop—you have that budget report to finish,” and I’m not even enjoying it anymore, but I keep eating anyway.
How often do these episodes of overeating happen—would you say it's about once a week, and if so, how long has this been going on?
Yeah, it’s usually more than once a week. I looked back at my journal and my food delivery charges, and it’s been happening most weeks since the restructuring started—not just once in a while.
When you think about these episodes of overeating, do you feel a lot of guilt, shame, or disgust with yourself about the eating itself, separate from any concerns about your weight?
I’m not really sure. I know I feel bad afterward, but I haven’t thought about whether it’s guilt or shame about the eating itself, exactly.
Would you say these episodes cause you significant distress or upset—like they weigh on your mind or bother you a lot—beyond just feeling physically uncomfortable afterward?
I’m not sure how to separate that out. I definitely don’t feel good afterward, but I haven’t really thought about how much it weighs on me beyond that.
Have you noticed any significant weight gain or physical health changes—like increased blood pressure, blood sugar issues, or joint pain—since this eating pattern started?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any big physical changes, and I haven’t had anything checked like blood pressure or blood sugar.
Do you ever eat alone or hide how much you're eating because you feel embarrassed by the amount of food you're consuming?

Yeah. I usually wait until my roommate is out, or until my family’s gone to bed. I’m embarrassed for anyone to see how much I’m eating, especially because during the day I act pretty put-together and health-conscious.
When did this restructuring at your job start—about how many months ago was that?
About four months ago, I think. It started around when the office restructuring happened and I began having those late-night reporting deadlines.
When you think about these episodes afterward, would you say they genuinely upset you or trouble you emotionally, distinct from feeling stuffed or uncomfortable physically?
I’m not really sure. I mean, afterward I mostly just notice that I feel physically uncomfortable. I haven’t really thought about whether it upsets me emotionally beyond that.
Aside from feeling physically stuffed afterward, do you ever feel disgusted with yourself, depressed, or very guilty specifically because of how much you ate during these episodes?
I don’t know. I mostly just feel uncomfortably full afterward. I haven’t really noticed those other feelings specifically.
During these episodes, do you notice yourself eating much faster than you normally would, almost gulping food down quickly?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to how fast I’m eating during them.
During these episodes, do you often find yourself eating a large amount of food even when you're not physically hungry at all?

Yeah, a lot of the time it happens right after I’ve already eaten dinner, when I’m not physically hungry. I still end up going back to the kitchen or ordering more food because my mind feels restless.
When you notice yourself unable to stop eating during these episodes, does that loss of control itself bother you or make you feel upset, separate from how full you feel afterward?

Yeah. Once I start, it’s like I’m watching myself keep reaching for the next thing while I’m thinking, “Jaime, stop.” I know I have a budget report to finish, and I’m not even enjoying it anymore, but I still keep eating.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes (more than once weekly for ~4 months) of eating objectively large amounts of food with a clear sense of loss of control, eating alone due to embarrassment, and eating in the absence of hunger. However, she does not clearly endorse other core associated features (eating much more rapidly than normal, marked subjective distress specifically about the eating itself, feelings of guilt/disgust/depression distinct from physical fullness).
